_comment: The published price of credit. This file is the single source: domain.js, the application form and the prose on the site are all checked against it by scripts/check-rates.mjs, so a change here is a change everywhere or CI fails. Served publicly on purpose — these rates are published.

terms._comment: Weeks to flat interest percent, applied once to the principal and never compounded.

overdue._comment: Applies when a loan passes its final due date. The band REPLACES the term rate rather than adding to it: a 4-week loan at 30% becomes 35% in total, not 65%.
overdue._capComment: Accrued interest stops at the principal, so the most anyone can owe is twice what they borrowed. This mirrors the in duplum rule applied across the region and keeps a forgotten loan from growing without limit. Confirm against whatever cap the Bank of Zambia sets under the Banking and Financial Services Act No. 9 of 2026 before relying on it.
overdue._knownGap: A 4-week loan settled at week eight carries the 40% band — K5,600 on K4,000 — against K5,800 for the 45% two-month product, so defaulting is K200 cheaper in that window. Parity arrives at week twelve, when the band reaches 45%. Raising startPercent to 40 would close the rest. Left as specified; asserted in tests/rates.test.mjs.
overdue._floorComment: The band never reduces what is owed. Because startPercent (35) is below the 8-week term rate (45), an 8-week loan would otherwise get K400 cheaper the day it went overdue. av_amount_owing() floors the applied rate at the term rate and reports heldAtTermRate when it does. An 8-week loan therefore carries no late charge until the band passes 45% at day 57 — if that is too lenient, the fix is a per-term start band, not removing the floor.
overdue._stepTiming: The band steps ON the boundary: 35% covers days 1-27, 40% starts on day 28 (week eight), 45% on day 56 (week twelve). This matches the ladder as specified — 35% at week four, 40% at week eight, 45% at week twelve.

legacy._comment: Loans signed before this file existed carry their own late terms in the record's late_payment_rate field, written at signing (7.5% per week overdue, additive, entered by staff). Those agreements are binding as signed. The engine never applies the ladder above to them.
